subject: Exploratory: Bento runtime SDK compatibility & lightweight certification
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@meadow.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro — Bento runtime SDK compatibility

Hi Soojin,

Quick intro — I’m Alice, product lead for integrations at Meadow Labs. We build Bento, a lightweight runtime for serving composition-first LLMs (embeddings + retrieval + small-chain orchestration). A few ISVs and consultancies (including LangChain partners) have asked for a first-class compatibility layer so they can drop in Bento as a runtime target.

We’d love to explore a small compatibility/certification path with Redwood so that LangChain/LlamaIndex SDKs and tracing tools can detect and optimally use Bento (prefix caching, KV semantics, token billing hooks, trace/span propagation).

High-level asks from our side:
- Simple SDK shim recommendations (LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters)
- Trace hook spec so distributed tracing and token attribution work end-to-end
- A lightweight test harness and checklist for a \"compatibility\" badge (docs + smoke tests)

I attached a rough integration spec and we can share a minimal runtime image for testing. Are you available for a 30‑minute discovery this week?

Thanks —
Alice Park
Product, Meadow Labs
Attachments: meadow-bento-integration-spec.md (overview, API surface, examples)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@meadow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — Bento runtime SDK compatibility

Hi Alice — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for the spec. This aligns with a lot of partner asks we’ve been tracking: ISVs want predictable fallback behavior and a clear way to route requests from LangChain/LlamaIndex to runtime variants.

I’d like to get Marissa (SDK integrations) and Jonas (runtime interop) on the call so we can scope a lightweight certification flow. Proposed time: Thu Apr 29 10:00am PT — does that work? If not, send a couple options and we’ll adjust.

Initial questions we’ll want answered on the call:
- How does Bento expose model selection and sequence-length hints?
- Are there tracing headers/span IDs we can consume?
- Do you have a small staging image / public endpoint for smoke tests?

Looping in Marissa and Jonas. Vanessa — I’ll copy you for commercial/partnership notes if you want to tag any program constraints.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Intro — Bento runtime SDK compatibility (internal prep)

FW: message from Meadow Labs (below).

Internal prep notes / proposed interop checklist for the call and quick POC:
1) API surface compatibility matrix
   - Tokenization / billing hooks: document header/param hooks (x-border-token-count)
   - Model variant mapping: how Bento exposes model aliases vs Redwood model catalog
   - Sequence-length and KV cache hints: expected behavior for prefix caching and cache invalidation
2) Tracing & attribution
   - Required trace/span header names (W3C traceparent, and a token-attribution header we can read)
   - How to attach call-level metadata for cost breakdown in Redwood Console
3) SDK shim points (LangChain + LlamaIndex)
   - Minimal adapter interface: send(request, ctx) -> {tokens, tokens_out, spans}
   - Sync/async streaming support and abort semantics
4) Test harness and acceptance criteria (interop-lite)
   - Smoke tests: model selection roundtrip, streaming stability, trace propagation, KV-prefetch behavior
   - Performance sanity: 95p latency within X ms of native Redwood runtime (for small-seq workloads)
   - Security checklist: inbound TLS, mTLS option if needed for private customers
5) Packaging & certification
   - Small docs pack + badge for "Redwood-compatible" when tests pass
   - Suggested rollout: alpha (ISV sandbox) -> beta (co-marketing) -> GA

Action items (proposal):
- Jonas: sniff runtime trace headers and confirm whether Bento exposes a span id in the example image (target: EOD Thu)
- Marissa: draft a small LangChain + LlamaIndex adapter spec and repo scaffold (target: Mon May 3)
- Vanessa: do we want a simple commercial notice (partner listing / co-marketing) or a formal certification program? Outline options (target: Mon May 3)

I attached a lightweight checklist we can iterate on during the call: interop-lite-checklist.md

— Soojin

On 2027-04-28 09:12, Alice Park <alice@meadow.ai> wrote:
> Hi Soojin,
> 
> Quick intro — I’m Alice, product lead for integrations at Meadow Labs...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Intro — Bento runtime SDK compatibility (internal prep)

This looks good — quick tactical notes from SDK side:

- Adapter surface: keep it tiny (3 functions): init(runtime_config), call(request, opts), stream(handler). We can reuse patterns from LangChain agent connectors to avoid doubling work.
- Trace propagation: we should standardize on W3C + an extra header 'x-redwood-cost-meta' for token attribution. Jonas, will Bento's example image pass that through to spans?
- Test harness: I suggest a single pytest-based suite that runs against their staging endpoint (container) and a small suite inside our SDK CI that runs the smoke tests. If they can provide a docker-compose with a sample index, we can run CI on PRs.

Timeline suggestion:
- Discovery call Thu 4/29 (confirm)
- POC scaffold + repo + basic smoke tests by Mon 5/03
- Internal review + alpha sandbox by Mon 5/17

Risks / questions to surface on call:
- Network model mapping (their alias -> our verified variant) — need clear mapping rules to avoid noisy fallbacks.
- Billing hooks consistency — we must ensure token counts are deterministic across runtimes for cost reporting.

I can take the adapter scaffold and initial tests. Jonas can own trace header validation. Vanessa, if we want to offer a light "compatibility" badge, I can draft the pass/fail criteria; otherwise happy to keep it an engineering-first effort.

—Marissa
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@meadow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — Bento runtime SDK compatibility

Alice — thanks again for the spec and for taking the time on the call. Short summary and next steps (mutual action plan attached):

Summary:
- Redwood will provide:
  1) a minimal LangChain + LlamaIndex adapter scaffold (open repo)
  2) a short smoke-test harness we can run in CI against your staging image
  3) a trace header mapping guide (W3C + x-redwood-cost-meta)
- Meadow will provide:
  1) a staging container with a sample index and basic model aliases
  2) clear trace header behavior and an endpoint for span validation

Next steps / timeline:
- Tue May 3: Marissa shares initial adapter scaffold repo (PR template + smoke tests)
- Tue May 3: Jonas posts findings on trace header pass-through (expected: yes)
- Fri May 14: alpha sandbox test pass target (both sides run interop-lite-checklist)

We attached a short mutual action plan PDF and the internal checklist for transparency: mutual-action-plan-meadow.pdf, interop-lite-checklist.md. Vanessa — please advise on partner listing / co-marketing once we hit alpha.

Alice — can you confirm the staging container link and share any access details (or a short docker-compose) so Marissa can wire up CI? Also, please confirm whether you want the badge to be public or partner-only.

Thanks — looking forward to this.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
Attachments: mutual-action-plan-meadow.pdf
